findings.evidence: The hypotheses at lines 139–140 give a bijective internal-sum map and equivalences `N i ≃ₗ Sl2Std K (n i)`; Mathlib's `Module.finrank_directSum` only requires finiteness of the summands, while `LinearEquiv.finrank_eq` itself has no finite-dimensional hypothesis.
findings.fix: Omit `[FiniteDimensional K M]`; transfer `Module.Finite` to each `N i` through `hn i`, use those instances for `Module.finrank_directSum`, and use the internal-sum equivalence directly for `M`.
findings.issue: `Sl2Std.finrank_eq_sum` inherits `[FiniteDimensional K M]`, although an internal finite decomposition whose summands are equivalent to finite-dimensional `Sl2Std K (n i)` already forces the needed finiteness.

summary: The dimension-count theorem carries an unnecessary finite-dimensionality assumption already implied by its decomposition data.
